question.text: A broker wants to start offering algorithmic trading services to clients for ETIRD. Before going live, what steps must be completed?

answer.text: Obtain prior stock exchange permission, implement minimum order-level risk controls (including price and quantity checks), route orders via broker servers located in India, undergo six-monthly system audit, and meet the applicable Algo BMC (Rs. 50 lacs)
Simply install the software and start trading
Obtain SEBI approval only; no exchange-level requirement
File a notification with the exchange after starting live trading

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires prior stock exchange permission for algo trading, implementation of order-level risk controls including price and quantity checks, six-monthly system audit, broker-server routing in India, and a BMC of Rs. 50 lacs for all brokers offering Algo. The Trap: Going live without exchange approval, treating SEBI approval as sufficient on its own, or notifying the exchange only after going live are all non-compliant. Material changes to the algo also require renewed checks. Note: Kill switches are listed as a general pre-trade control, not as a specific algo pre-live approval condition. Treat any "empanelled auditor" or specific pre-live kill-switch requirement as needing a separate source citation before relying on it.
